decision_points.question: Which type of statistical model estimates the adjusted skin-tone effect on red cards?
decision_points.why_rival: each is a full model-family spec (log-games logistic, negative-binomial GLMM, Poisson-offset, referee FE, binomial/mixed cascades) chosen as THE primary estimator; they don't co-occur with each other

decision_points.question: Which covariates does the adjusted model control for?
decision_points.why_rival: each names a single adjustment set (games only, position only, games+position, +league, log-games+minimal, etc.); an analyst picks one set for the primary model

decision_points.question: Does the model include a skin-tone × country-bias (IAT/exposure) interaction term?
decision_points.why_rival: main-effects-only vs interactions-included vs conditionally-included are rival answers to whether interaction terms enter the model

decision_points.question: Which correlation coefficient quantifies the bivariate skin-tone/red-card association?
decision_points.why_rival: Pearson vs Spearman are the two coefficient choices for the same correlational analysis and never co-occur

decision_points.question: How is the crude, unadjusted association quantified?
decision_points.why_rival: the crude risk-difference is a distinct descriptive-effect slot (co-occurs with correlations and regressions, so not their rival)

decision_points.question: Which reference year is used to compute age from birth year?
decision_points.why_rival: fixing 2012, 2013, or an unspecified year are mutually exclusive choices for the same subtraction

decision_points.question: How is the middle (Medium) skin-tone category handled?
decision_points.why_rival: dropping the Medium group to keep only Light/Dark is one answer to how the skin-tone categories are grouped

decision_points.question: How are the raters' skin-tone scores encoded numerically?
decision_points.why_rival: recoding each rater's score to a zero-based numeric scale settles how the categorical ratings become a numeric variable

decision_points.question: What criterion determines whether the effect is declared statistically supported?
decision_points.why_rival: bootstrap p<.05 vs CI-excludes-zero vs the disjunction of the two are rival decision rules for calling the hypothesis supported

decision_points.question: How is the p-value / uncertainty for the exposure effect obtained?
decision_points.why_rival: analytic Wald p-value vs two bootstrap p-value constructions are rival ways to produce the same inferential quantity

decision_points.question: How are bootstrap iterations whose model fit fails handled?
decision_points.why_rival: catching and dropping exception-throwing bootstrap draws settles how failed resamples are treated

decision_points.question: Are dyads with zero games excluded from the sample?
decision_points.why_rival: keeping games>=1 is one disposition of zero-game records

decision_points.question: Are referees who encountered only one player excluded?
decision_points.why_rival: dropping single-player referees settles who counts as sufficiently-observed

decision_points.question: Is the sample restricted to particular player positions?
decision_points.why_rival: restricting to Defender/Goalkeeper dyads settles which players the study is about

decision_points.question: Are referee-country fixed effects added to adjust for country?
decision_points.why_rival: including referee-country fixed effects settles whether country-level confounding is absorbed

decision_points.question: How is multicollinearity assessed?
decision_points.why_rival: computing VIF on the four continuous/base predictors settles the collinearity diagnostic

decision_points.question: Is a covariate-balance / descriptive table reported?
decision_points.why_rival: the games-and-yellow-cards balance table settles what descriptive balance check is presented

decision_points.question: Are model coefficients exponentiated to odds ratios for reporting?
decision_points.why_rival: exponentiating glmer fixed effects settles the scale on which effects are reported

decision_points.question: Is a confidence interval reported alongside the point estimate?
decision_points.why_rival: reporting the odds-ratio point estimate without a CI settles whether interval uncertainty is shown

decision_points.question: Is a model-fit comparison table across specifications produced?
decision_points.why_rival: assembling a cross-specification fit-statistics table settles whether models are compared side by side

decision_points.question: How is the source dataset loaded for the main analysis?
decision_points.why_rival: reloading the csv fresh via read_csv settles how the analysis data is ingested

decision_points.question: Under what condition is a position-subgroup model reported?
decision_points.why_rival: the >1000-observation threshold settles when a subgroup model is deemed reportable
